 Mountain Rescue Team Rescues German Brothers (13, 16) in South Tyrol
 -/Mountain Rescue Italy/dpa
 A family with two sons, ages 13 and 16, sets out on a hike. The parents turn back—and the boys find themselves in front of a locked cabin at an altitude of more than 2,300 meters.
 DPA 
 20.10.2026, 08:21 In South Tyrol, the mountain rescue service rescued two German brothers in the middle of the night after they became stranded alone at a closed mountain hut at an altitude of more than 2,300 meters. According to the mountain rescue service, the two boys, aged 13 and 16, had set out on a hike with their parents from Dobbiaco. However, the parents turned back after a few hours and let the boys continue on their own. Around 1:00 a.m., an emergency call was received because the boys were standing alone in front of the Bonnerhütte, which had already closed for the season. The mountain rescue service transported the two boys to the hospital.
 A spokesperson for the Pustertal Mountain Rescue Service told the German Press Agency that, after climbing more than 1,000 meters in elevation, the boys had become severely hypothermic due to the cold at that altitude. One of them had to vomit. They have since been discharged from the hospital.
 The cabin has been closed for a week now
 According to a report in the daily newspaper *Dolomiten*, the two were wearing hiking boots on the hike, which began on Saturday, but were not wearing appropriate clothing. The parents had agreed to let them spend the night at the hut because they considered their children experienced enough. However, it appears they did not check the hut’s operating hours.
 The Bonnerhütte has been closed for more than a week. It was built in 1897 by the Bonn chapter of the Alpine Club as a mountain shelter. The mountain rescue service did not provide any further details about the family’s background. The spokesperson for the mountain rescue service spoke of gross negligence. He added, “Fortunately, something like this happens only rarely.”
